clue.text: Artist, wearing frown, discount-. ing old careless writing

indicators.note: the frown is worn around the artist, so it wraps the artist's letters
discounting, broken by the print line, means leaving out the letter for old

parts.note: a scowl is a frown
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An elderly artist frowns while dismissing some old, careless handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discounting' leaves SCWL; 'wearing' means that frown goes round the artist. The newspaper print breaks 'discounting' across a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy, hurried handwriting, the very picture of careless penmanship.

clue.text: Shipment made by characters in ocean region regularly

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter from the words ocean region

explanation.surface: A shipment is assembled from goods found across an ocean region.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods a ship carries, a shipment in plain terms.

clue.text: Pay etcher poorly for pattern

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of pay etcher are badly arranged and must be reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pay an engraver a pittance for a design.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is an original model or pattern from which copies are made.

clue.text: Pretentious young man thought to lack energy

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: to lack energy means the letter for energy is dropped from the word for thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A young man is said to have no get-up-and-go and to be rather affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lack energy' removes E from IDEA, leaving IDA.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal adjective for affected, pretentious manners or speech.

clue.text: Cutting price for salt

parts.note: a cutting remark is tart, sharp
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: Someone is slashing the price of table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as reducing the price, but it is a synonym for sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartrate is a chemical salt of tartaric acid, as in cream of tartar.

clue.text: Give up list about haul found under hot terrace in shade

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is found under comes lower, so the list-and-haul part follows
the hot terrace sits in the shade, so those letters go inside the word for shade

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
a row is a terrace of houses

indicators.note: the list goes about the haul, wrapping its letters

parts.note: to heel is to list, as a ship leans
to tow is to haul

explanation.surface: A tired worker quits after a list of hauling chores on a shady hot terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found under' matters because this is a down entry: HETOWEL sits below THROWINT. In British usage a terrace is a row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing in the towel is a boxing idiom for conceding defeat, so it means to give up.

clue.text: Not absolute end of matter? Leave it unsettled

indicators.note: end of matter points to the last letter of that word
unsettled means the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says the end of the matter is not final, so leave the question open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of matter' gives R, which is shuffled with LEAVE IT by 'unsettled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative is the opposite of absolute, depending on comparison with something else.

clue.text: Trouble in service supplying gas

indicators.note: trouble sits in the service, inside its letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, a fighting service
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A fault in a utility service is cutting off the gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a utility, but it is the armed service, the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, a chemical element.

clue.text: Impractical man admitted to rushed, nervous action

indicators.note: the man is let into the word for rushed, inside it

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road
he stands for a man
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: An unrealistic man is rushed into some anxious action.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretic means concerned with theory rather than practice, so it is impractical.

clue.text: Mate stifling impolite utterance of surprise, on reflection, concerning method

indicators.note: the mate smothers what follows by enclosing it

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

indicators.note: on reflection says those words are read in mirror image, backwards

parts.note: rude means impolite
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A friend suppresses a rude gasp and thinks again about the method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' gives ROCEDUR, which 'stifling' encloses. Cor is a British exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedural describes what relates to procedure, the method of doing things.

clue.text: Expected large contest

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big contest was anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a fight or contest between two parties.

clue.text: Sweet stuff having colour, certainly not rejected, penned by hack

indicators.note: penned by means held inside the word for hack, enclosed as in a pen

parts.note: to hew is to hack, chop

indicators.note: rejected says these words are turned back, written in reverse

parts.note: a dye is a colour
no is a firm refusal, certainly not

explanation.surface: A hack writer turns down sugary prose with too much colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives ONEYD, which 'penned by' encloses after the first letter of the hack word. 'Sweet stuff' hides a sugary aphid secretion or a melon.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeydew is the sugary secretion of aphids, and also a sweet melon, so sweet stuff.

clue.text: Plain fish? Doctor's tucked into it

indicators.note: the doctor is placed inside the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plain fish dish is what the doctor is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' poses as describing the fish, but it is a noun: a flat treeless region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast flat treeless Arctic region, a type of plain.

clue.text: Psychic power variable in spot

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a psychic power
y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A medium's psychic gifts are uneven when put on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' is a verb here, to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, to spot it.

clue.text: Hint about entering wrong work area

indicators.note: the word for about goes into the word for wrong

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
c, for circa, means about
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A tip-off about someone straying into the wrong work zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, the barest hint of something.

clue.text: Guide in vain struggling with barrier

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of vain are thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: Someone tries in vain to steer through a gate they keep wrestling with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges VAIN into NAVI.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to direct a course, to guide a vessel or vehicle.

clue.text: Travel five hundred miles with different sponsor

parts.note: to go is to travel
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
other means different

explanation.surface: Someone travels a long way with a new backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Obedient, join up, enthralled by holy book

indicators.note: enthralled by means captured inside the holy book

parts.note: the Bible is the holy book

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for join is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to add is to join on

explanation.surface: A compliant person signs up, gripped by scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives DDA, which 'enthralled by' puts after the first two letters of the holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Biddable means docile and willing to do as bidden, so obedient.

clue.text: Malicious volume I pass on

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die, perish

explanation.surface: Someone hands on a spiteful book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' looks like handing something over, but here it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Viperish means venomous in manner like a viper, so spiteful and malicious.

clue.text: Cut tie up

definitions.meaning: to cut short, as a tail or wages
to moor a boat at a quay

explanation.definitionFit: Dock means to curtail, and also to bring a ship to berth and moor it.

clue.text: Drink, having laugh with companion

parts.note: a hoot is a burst of laughter
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink and a laugh with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour, hence companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hootch is slang for alcoholic liquor, especially cheap or illicit spirits.

clue.text: Sheep in team endlessly lacking sense

indicators.note: the sheep goes in the word for team
endlessly means the last letter of the word for team is dropped

parts.note: a side is a team
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep in a team that never stops is a dim creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' gives SID, and 'in' puts the ram inside. A tup is a British dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid means lacking intelligence or good sense, foolish.

clue.text: Idol not out to stop young boxer?

indicators.note: to stop here means to plug the middle of the word, filling it

parts.note: a boxer is a dog breed, so its young is a pup
in is the opposite of out, as a batsman still in

explanation.surface: A young prizefighter remains standing, the crowd's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young boxer' wants to be a fighter; it is a puppy of the boxer dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a person whose picture is pinned on a wall, an admired idol.

clue.text: Complete most of the round below par

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its last letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
feeling rough is feeling below par, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone finishes most of the golf round under par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH. 'below par' looks like golf scoring but means feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough means complete in every detail, utter.

clue.text: Kind and good before capturing

indicators.note: the word for before holds the word for and inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
n, as in rock 'n' roll, stands for and

explanation.surface: Someone is gentle and good before taking a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as an adjective but is a noun, a sort or type.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind, category or type, especially of art.

clue.text: Project necessary to stop landslide

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An engineering project is needed to halt a landslide.
explanation.definitionFit: A project is a scheme or plan, an undertaking proposed.

clue.text: Seductive humour, feature in appeal

indicators.note: humour and feature sit in the word for appeal

parts.note: to beg is to appeal
wit is humour
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A charming person's humour is a large part of their attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' poses as charm, but it is a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewitching means enchanting and alluring, so seductive.

clue.text: Rash leap injured aquatic mammal

indicators.note: injured means the letters of rash leap are damaged and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A creature hurts itself making a reckless jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp seal is an Arctic seal, a sea-dwelling mammal.

clue.text: Daughter in hurry to join new set

indicators.note: the daughter goes in the word for hurry

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, hurry

explanation.surface: A daughter rushes to join a fresh group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group joined, but it is a verb: to become firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden is to set firm, as concrete or jelly does.
